title: HostedAPI TTFB surge inspection notes
body:
Summary:

On 2029-06-11 ~15:12 UTC we observed a sharp p95/p99 TTFB (time-to-first-byte) increase for HostedAPI traffic affecting newly established streaming sessions and some fresh REST requests. The symptom set was a large number of requests returning slow first bytes (TTFB p95 went from ~120ms to ~2.2s and p99 to ~6s), while steady-state streaming deltas (after the first chunk) remained normal. Error rates (5xx) rose briefly for clients that timed out waiting for the first chunk. Impact was regional, concentrated in us-west-2 edge nodes. Estimated customer impact: increased latency and a small fraction of aborted streams (~0.7% of total sessions during the window).

Detection and alerts:

- Alert fired: SRE: HostedAPI TTFB p95 > 1.0s (3 consecutive 1m evals) at 2029-06-11 15:13 UTC.
- Pager on-call: Daniel (SRE) paged at 15:14 UTC.
- Slack alert channel received multiple customer complaints describing slow start.

Initial hypothesis and triage notes:

- Hypothesis A: Upstream model host cold-start or KV cache miss amplifying first-chunk work.
- Hypothesis B: Network congestion/egress path issues causing acceptor backlog and SYN queue.
- Hypothesis C: A new deploy introduced a blocking operation during session setup.

Triage steps taken (chronological):

1) 15:15 UTC - SRE ran cluster-wide p95/p50 breakdown by client_ip and route. Found skew towards new-session routes (/v1/stream and /v1/chat/completions with new-session header).
2) 15:18 UTC - Looked at edge pod telemetry: CPU and net were normal; acceptor queue length briefly rose on a subset of edge nodes.
3) 15:22 UTC - Correlated deployments: a deploy at 14:58 UTC to edge service "edge-conn-manager" introduced a background preflight check (session-preflight) that performed synchronous metadata lookups against service-md during connection establishment.
4) 15:28 UTC - Metrics from service-md showed slow DB response times (read path p99 ~1.2s). The DB's slow query logs showed a single query pattern with full table scan on metadata.tags after a code-path change in GH-PR-4821.
5) 15:34 UTC - Canary rollback of the edge-conn-manager preflight to previous image (kubectl set image on edge deployment) initiated.
6) 15:40 UTC - Rolling rollback completed to previous stable image across affected nodes. TTFB p95 returned to baseline within ~4min after the rollback finished.

Root cause (confirmed):

A synchronous session-preflight introduced in edge-conn-manager (deployed 14:58 UTC, GH-PR-4821) performed a blocking read against service-md to validate client session metadata. Service-md's schema had recently been updated by a separate change (non-canary) that caused the metadata.tags query to lose its index (query planner regression); under burst traffic the query p99 ballooned and the blocking preflight amplified the delay into user-visible TTFB spikes for new sessions. In short: a blocking preflight + regression in a frequently-used metadata query caused initial-setup latency amplification.

Why the symptom set looked like it did:

- Only new sessions and fresh REST calls hit the preflight path; long-lived sessions were unaffected.
- The preflight is synchronous and on the hot path for connection setup so DB latency directly increased TTFB.
- Edge nodes with higher new-session rates saw transient acceptor queue growth because setup was slowed per-connection, but CPU and network looked normal otherwise.

Immediate mitigation and timeline:

- 15:34 UTC: Initiated rollback of edge-conn-manager to v2029.06.07 (pre-change image).
- 15:40 UTC: Rollback finished; traffic rebalanced off affected pods.
- 15:44 UTC: TTFB p95 trending back to baseline; alerts auto-resolved by 15:49 UTC.

Longer-term fixes implemented during response:

- 15:55 UTC: Enabled temporary local in-process caching of session metadata in edge-conn-manager to provide fallback for the short term (TTL 30s). This was a conservative mitigator while root cause was validated.

Permanent remediation plan (actions in progress or scheduled):

1) Service-md DB index fix: Add missing index for metadata.tags query and re-run explain plans for the top 10 query patterns. Owner: Marina Ruiz (DB eng). ETA: 2029-06-18.
2) Make preflight asynchronous with circuit breaker: Convert session-preflight to async and use an immediate cached fallback on miss; add a circuit breaker to short-circuit when service-md p95 > 300ms. Owner: Ethan Li (edge team). ETA: 2029-06-20.
3) Canary gating for connection-path changes: Add automated canary checks for any synchronous call added to connection setup that measures 99th percentile impact on TTFB in the canary window. Owner: Priya Nair (platform QE). ETA: 2029-06-25.
4) Update runbook: Add a new playbook section for "session-preflight-induced TTFB" that lists detection queries and immediate rollback steps (see runbook snippet below). Owner: Aisha Kapoor. ETA: 2029-06-16.
5) Instrumentation: Add fine-grained telemetry on session-preflight latency and whether each session used a cached vs DB-backed preflight result. Owner: Edge observability. ETA: 2029-06-19.
6) Post-deploy automated slow-query scan: Scheduled job to run explain/analyze on top metadata queries after any DB schema/ORM change; failure blocks non-emergency deploys. Owner: DB platform. ETA: 2029-06-30.

Runbook snippet (for oncall):

- Detection queries (promql examples):
  - hostedapi_ttfb_p95{region="us-west-2"} > 1.0
  - edge_session_preflight_latency_p99 > 300ms
- Quick triage:
  - Check which routes have new-session header: rate(hostedapi_requests{header_session_new="true"})
  - Look for recent edge deployments: kubectl get deploy -n edge --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp | tail -n 20
  - Query service-md latency: sum(rate(service_md_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (quantile) and inspect slow query log on the DB host cluster-md-1
- Immediate mitigation options (ordered):
  1) Rollback edge-conn-manager to previous stable image (kubectl set image deployment/edge-conn-manager ...).
  2) If rollback is not possible, scale edge-conn-manager to reduce new-session pressure and route new sessions to canary-safe region via routing policy.
  3) Enable local in-process caching TTL=30s (toggle via feature-flag).

Post-incident notes and lessons learned:

- Risk controls: Adding any blocking external call to connection/session setup is high risk; we underestimated the blast radius of a DB query regression in a hot path.
- Testing gaps: The preflight was canaried in functional traffic but not measured for p99 TTFB impact for new sessions; our canary checks did not include a synthetic burst of new-session traffic.
- Ownership gaps: Schema/ORM change that removed the index was not linked clearly to service-md's performance owner; need tighter post-change verification.
- Observability: There was insufficient signal to attribute the TTFB to service-md until we correlated DB slow logs; add direct preflight call tracing to make root cause faster to find.

Action items (concrete):

- Marina: implement DB index, run explain plans, and post evidence to JIRA-8901. Due 2029-06-18.
- Ethan: implement async preflight + circuit breaker and a short-circuit cached path; open PR and include perf regression tests (add to GH-PR-5002). Due 2029-06-20.
- Priya: extend canary test harness to include new-session burst tests and add gating rules. Due 2029-06-25.
- Aisha: update SRE runbook pages and add the detection queries + mitigation steps to the oncall playbook. Due 2029-06-16.
- Observability team: add a dedicated metric edge_session_preflight_latency and a tracing span for the preflight call. Due 2029-06-19.

Open questions / follow-ups:

- Should session-preflight remain a feature at all, or should we push validation to a background task after session establishment? (ops/edge design discussion)
- What is an appropriate cache TTL that balances correctness and latency risk? (security/product input required)

Appendix: useful commands and places to look

- kubectl get deploy -n edge edge-conn-manager -o yaml
- kubectl rollout undo deployment/edge-conn-manager -n edge --to-revision=...
- Prometheus queries used: hostedapi_ttfb_p95{region=~"us-.*"}, edge_session_preflight_latency_bucket
- DB slow query path: ssh db-cluster-md-1 -> /var/lib/postgres/log/slow_query.log; sample pattern: SELECT * FROM metadata.tags WHERE key = $1 ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1; (missing index on key)
- GH PR that introduced preflight: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-conn-manager/pull/4821
- JIRA ticket for DB work: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/JIRA-8901

Tags for searchability: TTFB, session-preflight, rollback, DB-index, canary, edge-conn-manager

Notes written by: Aisha Kapoor (oncall lead).
